- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and forecast shows strong downward bias, reduce downward correction magnitude to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down then up), model should not overreact to new sentiment; dampen forecast volatility.  
- After a sharp spike in price (forecast > true), reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to account for lagged market correction.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.25) and forecast is trending sharply, apply a 3–5 day smoothing filter to avoid false momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend instead of 30-day trend.
